added_lemmas.statement:
For fixed \(\eta\in(0,1/2)\), fixed class parameters \(\alpha\in[0,1)\), \(\beta,L,c,\varepsilon>0\) satisfying the declared parameter restrictions, and any prespecified deterministic \(\Delta_T\geq0\), there exist constants \(0<c_\eta\leq C_\eta<\infty\) such that
\[
 \inf_{(P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}(\alpha,\beta,L,c,\varepsilon)}
 P\{\tau\in I_{T,\Delta}\}\geq1-\eta-o(1)
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{(P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}(\alpha,\beta,L,c,\varepsilon)}
 \mathbb E_{P,\Pi}|I_{T,\Delta}|\leq C_\eta r_{T,\Delta}.
\]
Conversely, every \(O_{T,\Delta}\)-measurable interval \(J_{T,\Delta}\) satisfying
\[
 \inf_{(P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}(\alpha,\beta,L,c,\varepsilon)}
 P\{\tau\in J_{T,\Delta}\}\geq1-\eta-o(1)
\]
obeys
\[
 \sup_{(P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}(\alpha,\beta,L,c,\varepsilon)}
 \mathbb E_{P,\Pi}|J_{T,\Delta}|\geq c_\eta r_{T,\Delta}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(T\). Here \(r_{T,\Delta}=\max\{T^{-(1-\alpha)/2},(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}\}\), and each expectation integrates over the independent and identically distributed outcome--delay arrivals under \(P\) and every randomization induced by the predictable policy \(\Pi\). Both converse components use the same fixed policy \(\pi_t(1)=ct^{-\alpha}\): prompt mean tilts give the sampling term, while finite hidden-sign delays at \(H_T+1\) give the tail term. Thus, at \(\Delta_T=0\), the exact class-minimax expected-length order is \(\max\{T^{-(1-\alpha)/2},T^{-\beta}\}\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(q=(1-\alpha)/2\). We first record the relation between the two design classes. If \((P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_T(\alpha,\beta,L,c,C,\varepsilon)\), then ass:rare-arm-envelope gives \(\pi_t(1)\geq ct^{-\alpha}\). Since there are two arms,
\[
 \pi_t(0)=1-\pi_t(1)
 \geq 1-Ct^{-\alpha}
 \geq1-C\geq\varepsilon. \tag{1}
\]
Thus ass:one-sided-forced-exploration and ass:control-floor hold, while the other defining assumptions are common to the two classes. By def:model-class and def:one-sided-policy-class,
\[
 \mathfrak M_T(\alpha,\beta,L,c,C,\varepsilon)
 \subseteq
 \mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}(\alpha,\beta,L,c,\varepsilon). \tag{2}
\]
In particular, the deterministic policy
\[
 p_t:=\pi_t(1)=ct^{-\alpha},
 \qquad \pi_t(0)=1-p_t, \tag{3}
\]
belongs to the one-sided class: its rare-arm inequality is an equality, and \(1-p_t\geq1-c\geq\varepsilon\). It also belongs to the contained two-sided class because \(c\leq C\).

\emph{Upper bound.}
The policy-uniform coverage assertion follows from thm:uniform-gated-inference, which applies on \(\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}\) without conditioning on quota success and without convergence of \(t^\alpha\pi_t(1)\). It remains to bound length. Put \(K_a=K_a(n_T)\) and
\[
 S_T=K_1^{-1}+K_0^{-1}.
\]
By lem:quota-success,
\[
 K_1\asymp T^{1-\alpha},\qquad K_0\asymp T,
 \qquad J_1\asymp T^{\rho(1-\alpha)},qquad J_0\asymp T^\rho, \tag{4}
\]
uniformly on the one-sided class. Hence
\[
 S_T=O(T^{-(1-\alpha)}),
 \qquad a_T=\sqrt{2S_Tx_\eta}=O(T^{-q}). \tag{5}
\]
Because \(g_{T,\Delta}=m_T+\Delta_T\geq m_T\asymp T^\rho\), ass:polynomial-delay-envelope and def:hybrid-interval give
\[
 v_{T,\Delta}=O(T^{-\rho\beta}). \tag{6}
\]
For every fixed \(x>0\), (4)--(6) imply
\[
 \begin{split}
 A_{1,T,\Delta}(x)
 &=O\!\left(T^{-\rho(\beta+1-\alpha)/2}
       +T^{-\rho(1-\alpha)}\right)=o(T^{-q}),\\
 A_{0,T,\Delta}(x)
 &=O\!\left(T^{-\rho(\beta+1)/2}+T^{-\rho}\right)=o(T^{-q}).
 \end{split} \tag{7}
\]
Indeed, the first equality is little-oh because
\(\rho(\beta+1-\alpha)>1-\alpha\) and \(\rho>1/2\), exactly the two strict restrictions in def:cohort-schedule. The arm-zero exponents are larger because \(1+\beta>1-\alpha+\beta\). The same strict inequalities absorb logarithms, so
\[
 d_{T,\Delta}
 =A_{1,T,\Delta}(4\log T)+A_{0,T,\Delta}(4\log T)
 =o(T^{-q}). \tag{8}
\]

For observations in \([-1,1]\), the usual unbiased sample variance is at most \(2\). Therefore, on \(E_T\),
\[
 \widehat s_{T,\Delta}^2\leq2S_T,
 \qquad \widehat s_{T,\Delta}=O(T^{-q}). \tag{9}
\]
Let \(z=z_{1-\eta/2}\). For \(u\geq0\), evaluate the defining coverage function for \(c_\eta(u)\) at \(u+z\):
\[
 \Phi(z)+\Phi(2u+z)-1
 \geq2\Phi(z)-1=1-\eta.
\]
Since that function is increasing in its critical-value argument,
\[
 c_\eta(u)\leq u+z,
 \qquad
 \widehat s_{T,\Delta}c_\eta(B_{T,\Delta}/\widehat s_{T,\Delta})
 \leq B_{T,\Delta}+z\widehat s_{T,\Delta}. \tag{10}
\]
The convention for \(\widehat s_{T,\Delta}=0\) is already included in def:hybrid-interval.

Next, \(h_{T,\Delta}=H_T-k_T\), \(H_T\geq T\), and \(k_T=O(T^\rho)\) with \(\rho<1\), so
\[
 \frac{1+h_{T,\Delta}}{1+H_T}
 =1-\frac{k_T}{1+H_T}=1+o(1) \tag{11}
\]
uniformly over deterministic \(\Delta_T\geq0\). Ass:bounded-outcomes, ass:polynomial-delay-envelope, and def:bias-radius therefore give
\[
 B_{T,\Delta}=O((1+H_T)^{-\beta}). \tag{12}
\]
Equations (5), (7), and (12) show that the concentration branch has length \(O(r_{T,\Delta})\) on \(E_T\); equations (8)--(10) and (12) give the same conclusion for the Gaussian branch. Intersecting either branch with \([-2,2]\) cannot increase its length. On \(E_T^c\), the interval has length \(4\), while lem:quota-success yields
\[
 4P(E_T^c)\leq16T^{-4}=o(T^{-q})=o(r_{T,\Delta}). \tag{13}
\]
Taking expectations proves the asserted uniform upper bound. This is precisely the lower-envelope achievability argument formerly isolated as a separate transfer proposition; merging it here removes any need for an upper allocation envelope in the construction.

\emph{Sampling converse.}
Use the single fixed policy (3), set \(D_t(a)=0\) for both arms, and set \(Y_t(0)=0\). For arm \(1\), define two independent and identically distributed arrival laws \(P_+\) and \(P_-\) by
\[
 P_+\{Y_t(1)=1\}=P_-\{Y_t(1)=-1\}=\frac{1+d_T}{2},
 \qquad
 d_T=\lambda Q_T^{-1/2},
 \qquad Q_T=\sum_{t=1}^T p_t, \tag{14}
\]
with the complementary probabilities on the other Rademacher value. Here \(0<\lambda<(1-2\eta)/(2\sqrt2)\) is fixed. Because \(\alpha<1\), integral comparison gives
\[
 Q_T\asymp T^{1-\alpha},\qquad d_T\asymp T^{-q}, \tag{15}
\]
and \(d_T<1\) for all sufficiently large \(T\). These laws satisfy ass:iid-arrivals, ass:bounded-outcomes, and ass:polynomial-delay-envelope; policy (3) satisfies the declared sequential randomization and overlap conditions. Hence both experiments lie in \(\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}\), and in fact in its contained two-sided subclass \(\mathfrak M_T\). Their causal targets are \(\tau_+=d_T\) and \(\tau_-=-d_T\).

Assignments and logged propensities have the same law in the two experiments. Conditional on \(W_t=0\), the observed record also has the same law; conditional on \(W_t=1\), the Hellinger affinity of the two Rademacher laws is \(\sqrt{1-d_T^2}\). Independence over arrivals and the deterministic policy therefore give the exact observed-experiment affinity
\[
 \begin{split}
 \operatorname{Aff}(P_+^{O},P_-^{O})
 &=\prod_{t=1}^T\left[1-p_t\{1-\sqrt{1-d_T^2}\}\right]\\
 &\geq1-\sum_{t=1}^Tp_td_T^2
 =1-\lambda^2, 
 \end{split} \tag{16}
\]
where \(1-\sqrt{1-x}\leq x\) for \(x\in[0,1]\) and
\(\prod_t(1-x_t)\geq1-\sum_tx_t\) for \(x_t\in[0,1]\). For any two dominated laws with affinity \(A\), Cauchy--Schwarz yields
\[
 \|P-Q\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 =\frac12\int|\sqrt p-\sqrt q|(\sqrt p+\sqrt q)
 \leq\sqrt{1-A^2}. \tag{17}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \|P_+^{O}-P_-^{O}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\leq\sqrt2\lambda. \tag{18}
\]

Let \(J_{T,\Delta}\) be uniformly honest on the one-sided class. Under \(P_+^{O}\), the union bound and (18) imply
\[
 P_+^{O}\{\tau_+\in J_{T,\Delta},\ \tau_-\in J_{T,\Delta}\}
 \geq1-2\eta-o(1)-\sqrt2\lambda. \tag{19}
\]
The right-hand side is eventually bounded below by a positive constant depending only on \(\eta\) and the chosen \(\lambda\). On this event the interval has length at least \(|\tau_+-\tau_-|=2d_T\). By (15),
\[
 \sup_{(P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}}
 \mathbb E_{P,\Pi}|J_{T,\Delta}|
 \geq c_{\eta,1}T^{-q}. \tag{20}
\]

\emph{Hidden-tail converse.}
Retain the same policy (3) and put
\[
 \delta_T=\min\{1/4,L(1+H_T)^{-\beta}\}. \tag{21}
\]
For each arrival and arm, independently draw a Bernoulli variable of success probability \(\delta_T\). On failure set \((Y_t(a),D_t(a))=(0,0)\). On success set \(D_t(a)=H_T+1\); under \(P_+\), set the successful outcome to \(+1\) in arm \(1\) and \(-1\) in arm \(0\), and under \(P_-\) reverse both signs. The vectors are independent and identically distributed over \(t\), all outcomes lie in \([-1,1]\), and every delay is finite. For every integer \(u\geq0\),
\[
 P_\pm\{D_t(a)>u\}
 =\begin{cases}
 \delta_T,&0\leq u\leq H_T,\\
 0,&u\geq H_T+1,
 \end{cases}
 \leq\min\{1,L(1+u)^{-\beta}\}, \tag{22}
\]
so the polynomial envelope holds. Thus both laws again belong to the one-sided class and, under policy (3), to its contained two-sided subclass.

No successful delayed atom is revealed by \(H_T\). The laws of the visible zero outcomes, missingness indicators, assignments, logged propensities, and hence the entire observed experiment \(O_{T,\Delta}\), are exactly identical under \(P_+\) and \(P_-\). This conclusion does not use outcome--delay independence: the hidden outcome sign is deliberately coupled to its delay. Nevertheless, the eventual causal contrasts are
\[
 \tau_+=2\delta_T,
 \qquad \tau_-=-2\delta_T. \tag{23}
\]
Under the common observed law, uniform honesty and a union bound give
\[
 P\{\tau_+\in J_{T,\Delta},\ \tau_-\in J_{T,\Delta}\}
 \geq1-2\eta-o(1). \tag{24}
\]
On this event \(|J_{T,\Delta}|\geq4\delta_T\). Since \(H_T\geq T\to\infty\), (21) equals \(L(1+H_T)^{-\beta}\) eventually, and therefore
\[
 \sup_{(P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}}
 \mathbb E_{P,\Pi}|J_{T,\Delta}|
 \geq c_{\eta,2}(1+H_T)^{-\beta}. \tag{25}
\]
The affinity identity (16) and the identical-law assertion preceding (23) are finite-\(T\) calculations, so the smallest finite experiments already validate the two converse mechanisms; neither invokes quota success, adaptive stopping, or propensity convergence.

Combining (20) and (25), and using
\(\max\{c_{\eta,1}x,c_{\eta,2}y\}\geq
\min\{c_{\eta,1},c_{\eta,2}\}\max\{x,y\}\), proves the lower bound with \(r_{T,\Delta}=\max\{T^{-q},(1+H_T)^{-\beta}\}\). Finally, \(H_T=T\) when \(\Delta_T=0\), which gives the stated zero-follow-up frontier.
added_lemmas.justification: The deterministic lower-envelope quotas give one procedure with the stated uniform length on the full one-sided class, while a single fixed policy in its contained two-sided subclass supplies both matching converse experiments.
added_lemmas.gap: Existing delayed adaptive-inference results use a one-sided exploration floor together with outcome--delay independence; they do not give a uniformly honest expected-length frontier when the unobserved endpoint sign may depend on its delay.
added_lemmas.consumer: Investigators can translate a logged exploration floor, a control-arm floor, and an endpoint-tail audit into the shortest defensible order of uncertainty for the eventual treatment contrast.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The two-sided-class theorem is true but strictly subsumed by the proved one-sided-class theorem; replacement is the schema-valid way to upgrade rather than mislabel a strengthening as a narrowing.

proposed_core_edits.name: Mreg
proposed_core_edits.reason: The regular subfamily is now based on the full one-sided forced-exploration class, so its symbol references must point to that class.

The proved studentization argument uses only the lower-envelope quotas and the control-arm floor. Defining the regular class over the one-sided policy class propagates the valid stronger scope to the Gaussian calibration and Wald boundary.

prose_updates.tldr: Under the published one-sided polynomial exploration regime—\(\pi_t(1)\geq ct^{-\alpha}\) together with a control-arm floor—and allowing the endpoint and its finite delay to be arbitrarily dependent subject to the known envelope \(L(1+u)^{-\beta}\), a measurable two-cohort gate-and-fallback interval for the eventual arm-mean contrast has exact class-minimax expected-length order \(\max\{T^{-(1-\alpha)/2},(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}\}\). A fixed admissible policy supplies both matching converse experiments. The ordinary-Wald boundary is the vanishing tail-envelope-to-standard-error ratio, and the bounded-shift Gaussian critical value is attained at the phase boundary.

project_justification.gap: Delayed adaptive-inference theory treats one-sided forced exploration but centers scores using outcome--delay independence; reward-dependent-delay theory supplies regret lower bounds rather than uniformly honest intervals for an eventual causal contrast.
project_justification.niche: The missing design-based object is the exact expected-length frontier under the one-sided exploration allocation regime when logged propensities may oscillate, revelation is informative, and prespecified post-recruitment follow-up changes the observed endpoint set.
project_justification.fill: The project combines an unconditional arm-tape reduction, deterministic shifted two-cohort prefixes, an observable variance gate with a concentration fallback, and same-policy prompt-tilt and hidden-sign experiments to prove the frontier, the ordinary-Wald boundary, and the follow-up elbow.

sampling_model.treatment: The prespecified rare arm satisfies \(\pi_t(1)\geq ct^{-\alpha}\), and the control arm satisfies \(\pi_t(0)\geq\varepsilon\). Policies may allocate the designated arm more often than order \(t^{-\alpha}\). The former two-sided comparability class remains a contained hard subclass because \(ct^{-\alpha}\leq\pi_t(1)\leq Ct^{-\alpha}\) implies the control floor when \(C\leq1-\varepsilon\).
sampling_model.overlap: The headline class uses the one-sided polynomial forced-exploration floor plus the control-arm floor. Lower-envelope quotas give policy-uniform achievability even when \(t^\alpha\pi_t(1)\) does not converge; a single fixed policy \(\pi_t(1)=ct^{-\alpha}\) inside the class fixes the hard information order for the class-minimax converse.

prose_updates.related_work: Shi, Wang, and Wu provide the design-side anchor through a one-sided polynomial forced-exploration condition. The present result uses that allocation regime but extends inference to outcome-dependent delays, so it does not claim to cover their full outcome--delay-independence model as a special case in the converse direction: the hidden-sign tail witness deliberately lies outside that independence subclass. Hadad et al. and Bibaut et al. develop predictable weighting and variance stabilization for prompt outcomes. Manegueu et al. and Vernade et al. motivate polynomial delay-tail control under more restrictive delay structures. Lancewicki et al. and Tang, Wang, and Zheng analyze reward-dependent-delay bias and regret rather than interval length. Bai, Hu, and Rosenberger and Ma, Wang, and Wei obtain classical delayed response-adaptive asymptotics under ignorable-delay conditions. Armstrong and Kolesár provide the bounded-bias Gaussian calibration adapted to the attained boundary here. Liberali et al. are the cardiovascular-trial consumer: their real-time delayed-endpoint intervals need either a tail pad or follow-up sufficient for the uniform boundary, unless a stronger prompt or ignorable-delay law is separately certified.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The order frontier, uniform gate theorem, and attained bounded-shift calibration are proved, but exact normalized expected-length constants and the globally optimal variable-length or randomized interval remain open. The construction intentionally discards assignments beyond deterministic quotas, so it is order-optimal rather than constant-efficient for policies that explore more aggressively. Uniform validity uses a known tail envelope, independent and identically distributed stationary arrival vectors, bounded outcomes, finite delays implied by the polynomial envelope, and a prespecified terminal time; unknown envelope parameters, cross-arrival dependence, and nonstationary endpoint rates are outside scope.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The exact minimax order is over the one-sided forced-exploration class with a control-arm floor, not merely over the two-sided comparable-policy subclass. The same fixed policy \(\pi_t(1)=ct^{-\alpha}\) is used in both lower-bound pairs. The informative hidden-sign converse is not claimed for the outcome--delay-independence subclass of the anchor paper. On regular variance sequences, ordinary Wald is uniformly honest exactly when \(T^q(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}\to0\), where \(q=(1-\alpha)/2\). Consequently no follow-up is needed when \(\beta>q\); when \(\beta=q\), one needs \(\Delta_T/T\to\infty\); and when \(\beta<q\), one needs \(T+\Delta_T\gg T^{q/\beta}\). Outside this boundary the bias-aware Gaussian branch or concentration fallback supplies coverage. Application to a particular cardiovascular trial still requires an audit of stationarity, logged propensities, the tail envelope, terminal ascertainment, and the risk-difference estimand.

statement_notes.justification: The construction uses only lower-envelope quotas, while honesty over the larger class restricts to the contained fixed-policy hard experiments for the converse.
statement_notes.gap: The allocation floor from delayed adaptive-inference work has not previously been paired with an informative-delay same-experiment lower bound for uniformly honest interval length.
statement_notes.consumer: The result turns a logged exploration floor and endpoint-tail envelope into an exact order for the shortest uniformly defensible confidence interval.
